question: At an intersection of two lines, two angles are vertically opposite. If one of the angles measures 45°, what is the measure of the other angle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two straight lines intersect, the vertically opposite angles are always equal in measure.

Since one of the angles is given as 45°, its vertically opposite angle must exactly be 45°.

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One angle at the intersection of two lines = 45°.
